topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the lecture on how immune components coordinate the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and damage recognition by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and receptor pathways used by the innate immune system to detect signs of infection and cellular damage.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator release, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how innate immune activation drives cellular signaling, leukocyte migration to tissues and lymph nodes, and potentially dangerous systemic consequences.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system terminates inflammatory responses, repairs damaged tissue, and manages persistent insults through chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic for the next lecture.
